image_description: A realistic photograph of a grey whale surfacing in dark blue ocean water. The image captures the dorsal side of the whale, showing its mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches and a series of dorsal knuckles (humps) along the back where a dorsal fin would be on other species. The head is partially visible on the left, and the body extends towards the right, fading into the waves. No flippers or tail flukes are clearly visible above the water line.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially submerged and viewed from a high angle; the rostrum shape and blowholes are not clearly visible due to water reflection and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the back clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white patches consistent with barnacle infestations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a series of small humps (knuckles) along the ridge of the back instead of a single triangular dorsal fin, which is a key identifier for grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale, though the full length is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint, the body skin exhibits the correct texture and coloration patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is closed and submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external surfacing shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral sides and are completely submerged/obscured by the viewing angle and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is not visible in the frame; only the mid-to-posterior back is shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface texture appears uneven and rough, consistent with the presence of callosities and barnacles described in the taxonomy.
